brief: A compact walk through the three embedded extensions that matter most: C (compressed, 15 to 30 percent smaller code), E (16 registers for tiny MCUs), and M (hardware multiply and divide). If you are picking a core for a constrained board, this is the ten-minute version of the decision you will actually make.
title: RISC-V extensions for high performance embedded computing

brief: A field SOP for getting firmware off a device: triple-read every flash dump with flashrom and compare hashes, probe UART at 115200 8N1, drive JTAG through OpenOCD with concrete commands. The habit that matters is the triple read and hash compare, cheap insurance against a flaky clip corrupting your only copy.
title: Firmware reverse engineering SOP: acquisition, extraction, analysis

brief: The GCC 13 line is now closed: 265+ bug fixes since 13.4 and no more releases, so if your embedded toolchain is pinned to GCC 13, this is the final stop before planning the jump.
title: GCC 13.5 Released

brief: A two-stage int8 neural TTS pipeline running bare-metal across both cores of a CH32H417, from 85x slower than real time to 1.24x: the standout lesson is that staging one 16KB weight tap into RAM beat every arithmetic optimization combined, with the measurements to prove it.
title: rvTTS: Offline Neural TTS for RISC-V MCUs

brief: Patched OpenOCD for AG32 RISC-V debug through ADIv5 DAP, shipped as reproducible multi-platform binaries with matching SHA-256s, pinned source, and an SBOM: a clean example of how to publish open tooling for an obscure RISC-V part.
title: AGaMEMnon OpenOCD 0.1.0

brief: Ledger Donjon beat the RP2350's glitch detection, which stops ordinary voltage glitching, by decapping the chip on the back side and flipping the debug-enable register with an IR laser aimed by photon-emission microscopy. After a reset they read out the 128-bit secret Raspberry Pi had hidden in memory. The bench cost $250,000: with the hardware, the only question is how much effort it takes.
title: Laser Your Way Into Debug Mode On The RP2350

brief: Canonical maps what comes after RVA23: CFI (Zicfilp landing pads plus Zicfiss shadow stacks, designed to degrade gracefully where hardware lacks them), the matrix options (IME, VME, AME) with what each demands from the OS at context switch, and RVA23.1's new development and expansion options. The clearest single reference for which extensions your toolchain and kernel will need to handle next.
title: Evolution of the RISC-V ISA. What next after RVA23?

brief: AMD's ROCm 10.0 stack ran on a RISC-V host for the first time: 32 P870-D cores at 2.0 GHz driving Radeon AI PRO R9700 GPUs for Gemma 4 E2B inference offload on SiFive's BigSky SF-2U870 platform, demoed live at the AI Infra Summit. The takeaway for a working engineer: RISC-V is now a credible head node for GPU compute, which changes the porting calculus for every CUDA-first workload.
title: SiFive and AMD Collaborate to Optimize AMD ROCm on RISC-V Datacenter Servers

brief: Matthew "wrongbaud" Alt shows how to pull firmware from a device you cannot desolder: identify the boot-time SPI reads on a logic analyzer, decode the capture with Scapy into an image, and load it into binwalk. You only get what the CPU reads at boot, so the dump is incomplete by design, but the SPI protocol walkthrough alone is worth ten minutes for reverse engineers.
title: Reconstructing Device Firmware From SPI Reads

brief: Espressif's new HMI kit pairs the dual-core 320MHz RISC-V ESP32-S31 with a 2.16-inch 480x480 AMOLED touch display, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, and 802.15.4, plus a full ESP-IDF board support package. The value for engineers is the detailed hardware breakdown: named display, touch, audio, and power-management controllers to study before committing to the platform.
title: ESP-Mosaico centers dual-core RISC-V ESP32-S31 around a 2.16-inch square AMOLED

brief: Researchers irradiated ordinary electronics with an RF signal tuned to their internal unintentional antennas, turning amplifiers, ADCs, and converters back into effective TEMPEST transmitters. Worth reading if you design or audit secure hardware, because the attack moves the threat model from expensive lab setups to a USRP B210.
title: Reviving TEMPEST Attacks With An Injected Signal
Linux Finally Making It Easier To Answer The Question: 'Is This RISC-V System RVA23?'
brief: Kernel patches add a one-shot boot-time check for the RVA23 profile, so ISA-dependent kernel code can ask the hardware what it supports instead of guessing.

title: Auto Vectorizing The RISC-V Linux Kernel Shows Promising Results
brief: LPC 2026 numbers on building the RISC-V kernel with RVV auto-vectorization, up to 15 percent on LZ4, with honest accounting of the context-switch and portability costs.

title: Ubuntu 26.10 To Include Desktop Images For RISC-V
brief: First official Ubuntu desktop ISOs for RISC-V, with Xubuntu Minimal as the practical pick for QEMU, the fastest route to a working RISC-V userland for testing.

title: SpacemiT RISC-V SoCs To See More Improvements With Linux 7.4
brief: Upstream device-tree work for Linux 7.4 brings cpufreq, thermal and fan control to SpacemiT K1 and K3 boards like the Orange Pi RV2.

title: OpenSBI Firmware and U-Boot on RISC-V: Build Your Own
brief: Walks the full RISC-V boot chain on qemu-riscv64: OpenSBI firmware types, the S-mode handoff, and the load-address agreement with U-Boot.

title: HPMicro HPM5100 RISC-V MCU integrates four 16-bit ADCs, four op-amps for analog sensing and motor control
brief: 400 MHz RV32 MCU with integrated 16-bit ADCs, op-amps, and CAN FD, plus an open-source SDK, aimed at analog-heavy motor control designs.

title: Efinix Brings 64-Bit RISC-V Performance to Embedded FPGA Designs With New Sapphire RV64 SoC
brief: VexiiRiscv-based 64-bit soft core for Efinix FPGAs with SV39 and custom-instruction hooks, a path to Linux-capable RV64 in fabric.

title: mmRISC-2
brief: A home-made RV64GC core with caches, FPU, and JTAG debug that boots Linux to a shell on an Arty A7, with full bring-up notes.

A $7 ESP32-S3 board poses as a USB mouse and keyboard to drive a stock iPhone, no jailbreak needed. The repo ships a working AirPlay receiver port, BLE protocol notes, and pointer calibration, a reproducible lesson in how USB HID trust and accessibility features become a real input channel for hardware agents.
title: ESP32 iPhone Agent

brief: The capstone of a three-part series that builds a complete signed bootloader for STM32F0 with Ed25519 from Monocypher: the host-side signing tool, key handling, and packed footer format spelled out line by line. The stage, verify, then jump flow is the clearest working secure-boot reference outside a vendor app note.
title: Signing Firmware for a Secure Bootloader

brief: Pulls a live compressed instruction trace off an STM32F401 using only OpenOCD, a $10 logic analyzer, and Pulseview, instead of a multi-thousand-dollar trace probe. The two real failure modes, a PLL that moved the SWO baud and firmware that stole the SWO pin for I2C, are the parts worth reading twice.
title: Following the Instructions: Live ARM Tracing with the ETM, ITM, and TPIU

brief: An open-hardware iCE40 UltraPlus board whose bootloader can hold four bitstreams that boot each other, built for the all-open-source yosys/nextpnr toolchain. A genuine entry point for soft-core or CPU-less FPGA work with no vendor IDE in the loop.
title: Wenzel Labs' bare_metal Is a Lattice iCE40 FPGA Board with a Twist: Four Transputational Bitstreams

brief: Frank Denis shows with Compiler Explorer repros that LLVM silently emits data-dependent branches for hand-written constant-time code on RISC-V, and that the branch came and went across clang 15 through 23. The concrete fix is Zicond czero.eqz/nez, with an easy-to-miss Zkt timing caveat, plus honest limits of the asm barrier workaround.
title: Branches in branch-free code

brief: A patch series hardens eighteen BFD linker backends, RISC-V included, against an unsigned underflow in the in-place byte-deletion path that turned bad relocations into near-SIZE_MAX memmoves. Malformed objects now fail with a clear diagnostic instead of corrupting the linker heap.
title: Binutils hardens 18 ELF linkers against relaxation heap corruption

brief: The Zibi extension, compare-register-with-immediate branches (BEQI/BNEI), is in its 30-day public review before ratification, with LLVM data showing fewer spills and fewer dynamic instructions. The v0.99 spec PDF is public and feedback is open now, the last chance to shape a real ISA extension.
title: Public review for the Branch with Immediate (Zibi) extension

brief: A from-scratch walkthrough of instantiating Altera's RISC-V Nios V/m soft core on Agilex 3, including the exact reset wiring mistake that breaks debugging and a real linker-region-overflow fix. The scriptable CLI BSP build flow with the bundled riscv32-unknown-elf toolchain is the part worth stealing.
title: Building a Nios V soft processor system on the Agilex 3 dev kit
SpacemiT Announces The V100 Server-Class RISC-V Processor
brief: A 46-core hybrid server chip (six XiangShan cores plus forty SpacemiT X100 cores) claiming full RISC-V server-spec compliance, which would make it the first RISC-V part mainstream Linux distros can boot unmodified. Watch the spec-compliance claim, not the core count: it is what decides whether server software just works.

title: Linux 7.4 Kernel Crypto Library Enjoying Optimized AES Implementations On x86 and RISC-V
brief: Optimized RISC-V AES modes move from per-architecture crypto trees into the shared lib/crypto library, so in-kernel callers like dm-crypt finally get hardware acceleration instead of only skcipher users. It also deletes a pile of duplicated glue code from the RISC-V tree.

title: A RISC-V hypervisor in slow motion: XCP-ng and Xen Orchestra, from inside QEMU
brief: A field report on getting a full Xen-based virtualization stack (XCP-ng host, Xen Orchestra management, Docker and K3s guests) running on emulated RISC-V in QEMU. No real board yet, but it maps exactly where the RISC-V hypervisor story stands today.

title: gtrace v2: RISC-V Hardware Trace Rebuilt on the Generic Trace Framework (24-Patch RFC)
brief: A 24-patch RFC rewrites RISC-V hardware trace support onto the architecture-neutral gtrace framework instead of bending it into Arm CoreSight's device model, verified on a SpacemiT K3. If it lands, RISC-V and Arm trace would share one kernel path and one perf AUX pipeline.
